title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from new international partnerships to significant budget increases. Meanwhile, some projects are hitting snags, reminding us that not all launches go as planned.

themes.title: Artemis Accords Expansion
themes.body: With Mauritius signing on, the Artemis Accords now boast 70 nations. This growing coalition underscores a collective interest in lunar exploration, though the real question remains whether these nations will contribute tangible assets or just goodwill.

themes.title: Space Force Budget Boost
themes.body: The Space Force's FY27 budget markup includes a $1.4 billion increase for space resilience. This suggests a recognition of the escalating threats in orbit, although one wonders if more money will truly translate into more effectiveness.

themes.title: Launch Contract Ceiling Triples
themes.body: The Space Force has tripled its launch contract ceiling, reflecting a surge in demand for satellite deployments. However, one can't help but wonder if this is a sign of robust growth or just a reaction to a backlog of delayed launches.

themes.title: Hypersonic Test Delays Persist
themes.body: For the third consecutive quarter, a hypersonic glide-vehicle test has slipped. This recurring issue raises eyebrows about the pace of innovation in a field where speed is literally of the essence.
